verses.original: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς εἰ δὲ μή¦γε μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ Πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
verses.transliteration: Prosechete de tēn dikaiosynēn hymōn mē poiein emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn pros to theathēnai autois ei de mē¦ge misthon ouk echete para tō Patri hymōn tō en tois ouranois
verses.literal: Be careful - not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them If you do . . . you will have no reward from your Father in heaven

verses.original: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Hotan oun poiēs eleēmosynēn mē salpisēs emprosthen sou hōsper hoi hypokritai poiousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais rhymais hopōs doxasthōsin hypo tōn anthrōpōn amēn legō hymin apechousin ton misthon autōn
verses.literal: So when you give to the needy . . . do not sound a trumpet . . . before you as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets to be honored by men Truly I tell you they already have their full reward

verses.original: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου
verses.transliteration: sou de poiountos eleēmosynēn mē gnōtō hē aristera sou ti poiei hē dexia sou
verses.literal: But when you give to the needy . . . do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing

verses.original: ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι
verses.transliteration: hopōs ē sou hē eleēmosynē en tō kryptō kai ho Patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi
verses.literal: so that your giving may be in secret And your Father who sees what is done in secret will reward you

verses.original: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai hotan proseuchēsthe ouk esesthe hōs hoi hypokritai hoti philousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais gōniais tōn plateiōn hestōtes proseuchesthai hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois amēn legō hymin apechousin ton misthon autōn
verses.literal: And when you pray do not be . . . like the hypocrites For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men Truly I tell you they already have their full reward

verses.original: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ Πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι
verses.transliteration: sy de hotan proseuchē eiselthe eis to tameion sou kai kleisas tēn thyran sou proseuxai tō Patri sou tō en tō kryptō kai ho Patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi
verses.literal: But when you pray go into your inner room shut your door and pray to your Father who is unseen And your Father who sees what is done in secret will reward you

verses.original: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται
verses.transliteration: Proseuchomenoi de mē battalogēsēte hōsper hoi ethnikoi dokousin gar hoti en tē polylogia autōn eisakousthēsontai
verses.literal: And when you pray do not babble on . . . like pagans for they think that by their many words they will be heard

verses.original: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: mē oun homoiōthēte autois oiden gar ho Patēr hymōn hōn chreian echete pro tou hymas aitēsai auton
verses.literal: Do not be like them for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him

verses.original: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς Ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου
verses.transliteration: Houtōs oun proseuchesthe hymeis Pater hēmōn ho en tois ouranois Hagiasthētō to onoma sou
verses.literal: So then this is how you should pray Our Father in heaven hallowed be Your name

verses.original: Ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου Γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου Ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς
verses.transliteration: Elthetō hē basileia sou Genēthētō to thelēma sou Hōs en ouranō kai epi gēs
verses.literal: Your kingdom come Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven

verses.original: Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον
verses.transliteration: Ton arton hēmōn ton epiousion dos hēmin sēmeron
verses.literal: Give us this day our daily bread

verses.original: Καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν Ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai aphes hēmin ta opheilēmata hēmōn Hōs kai hēmeis aphēkamen tois opheiletais hēmōn
verses.literal: And forgive us our debts as we also have forgiven our debtors

verses.original: Καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν Ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai mē eisenenkēs hēmas eis peirasmon Alla rhysai hēmas apo tou ponērou
verses.literal: And lead us not into temptation but deliver us from the evil one

verses.original: Ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος
verses.transliteration: Ean gar aphēte tois anthrōpois ta paraptōmata autōn aphēsei kai hymin ho Patēr hymōn ho ouranios
verses.literal: For if you forgive men their trespasses your heavenly Father will also forgive . . . you

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν οὐδὲ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: ean de mē aphēte tois anthrōpois ta paraptōmata autōn oude ho Patēr hymōn aphēsei ta paraptōmata hymōn
verses.literal: But if you do not forgive . . . men their trespasses neither will your Father forgive yours . . .

verses.original: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Hotan de nēsteuēte mē ginesthe hōs hoi hypokritai skythrōpoi aphanizousin gar ta prosōpa autōn hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois nēsteuontes amēn legō hymin apechousin ton misthon autōn
verses.literal: When you fast do not be somber like the hypocrites for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting Truly I tell you they already have their full reward

verses.original: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι
verses.transliteration: sy de nēsteuōn aleipsai sou tēn kephalēn kai to prosōpon sou nipsai
verses.literal: But when you fast anoint your head and wash your face

verses.original: ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ Πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι
verses.transliteration: hopōs mē phanēs tois anthrōpois nēsteuōn alla tō Patri sou tō en tō kryphaiō kai ho Patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryphaiō apodōsei soi
verses.literal: so that your fasting will not be obvious . . . to men but only to your Father who is unseen And your Father who sees what is done in secret will reward you

verses.original: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν
verses.transliteration: Mē thēsaurizete hymin thēsaurous epi tēs gēs hopou sēs kai brōsis aphanizei kai hopou kleptai dioryssousin kai kleptousin
verses.literal: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth where moth and rust destroy and where thieves break in and steal

verses.original: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν
verses.transliteration: thēsaurizete de hymin thēsaurous en ouranō hopou oute sēs oute brōsis aphanizei kai hopou kleptai ou dioryssousin oude kleptousin
verses.literal: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven where moth and rust do not destroy and . . . where thieves do not break in . . . and steal

verses.original: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου
verses.transliteration: hopou gar estin ho thēsauros sou ekei estai kai hē kardia sou
verses.literal: For where your treasure is there your heart will be also

verses.original: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται
verses.transliteration: Ho lychnos tou sōmatos estin ho ophthalmos ean oun ē ho ophthalmos sou haplous holon to sōma sou phōteinon estai
verses.literal: The eye is the lamp of the body If your eyes are good your whole body will be full of light

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν τὸ σκότος πόσον
verses.transliteration: ean de ho ophthalmos sou ponēros ē holon to sōma sou skoteinon estai ei oun to phōs to en soi skotos estin to skotos poson
verses.literal: But if your eyes are bad your whole body will be full of darkness If then the light within you is darkness how great is that darkness

verses.original: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει οὐ δύνασθε Θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ
verses.transliteration: Oudeis dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein ē gar ton hena misēsei kai ton heteron agapēsei ē henos anthexetai kai tou heterou kataphronēsei ou dynasthe Theō douleuein kai mamōna
verses.literal: No one can serve two masters Either he will hate the one and love the other or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other You cannot . . . serve both God and money

verses.original: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε ἢ τί πίητε μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος
verses.transliteration: Dia touto legō hymin mē merimnate tē psychē hymōn ti phagēte ē ti piēte mēde tō sōmati hymōn ti endysēsthe ouchi hē psychē pleion estin tēs trophēs kai to sōma tou endymatos
verses.literal: Therefore . . . I tell you do not worry about your life what you will eat or drink or about your body what you will wear Is not life more than food and the body more than clothes

verses.original: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: emblepsate eis ta peteina tou ouranou hoti ou speirousin oude therizousin oude synagousin eis apothēkas kai ho Patēr hymōn ho ouranios trephei auta ouch hymeis mallon diapherete autōn
verses.literal: Look at the birds of the air They do not sow . . . or reap or gather into barns and yet your heavenly Father feeds them Are you not much more valuable than they

verses.original: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα
verses.transliteration: tis de ex hymōn merimnōn dynatai prostheinai epi tēn hēlikian autou pēchyn hena
verses.literal: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life

verses.original: Καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai peri endymatos ti merimnate katamathete ta krina tou agrou pōs auxanousin ou kopiōsin oude nēthousin
verses.literal: And why do you worry about clothes Consider how the lilies of the field grow They do not labor or spin

verses.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων
verses.transliteration: legō de hymin hoti oude Solomōn en pasē tē doxē autou periebaleto hōs hen toutōn
verses.literal: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these

verses.original: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ Θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς ὀλιγόπιστοι
verses.transliteration: ei de ton chorton tou agrou sēmeron onta kai aurion eis klibanon ballomenon ho Theos houtōs amphiennysin ou pollō mallon hymas oligopistoi
verses.literal: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace will He not much more clothe you O you of little faith

verses.original: Μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες Τί φάγωμεν ἤ Τί πίωμεν ἤ Τί περιβαλώμεθα
verses.transliteration: Mē oun merimnēsēte legontes Ti phagōmen ē Ti piōmen ē Ti peribalōmetha
verses.literal: Therefore do not worry saying What shall we eat or What shall we drink or What shall we wear

verses.original: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων
verses.transliteration: panta gar tauta ta ethnē epizētousin oiden gar ho Patēr hymōn ho ouranios hoti chrēzete toutōn hapantōn
verses.literal: For the Gentiles strive after all these things and your heavenly Father knows that you need them

verses.original: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: zēteite de prōton tēn basileian tou theou kai tēn dikaiosynēn autou kai tauta panta prostethēsetai hymin
verses.literal: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness and all these things will be added unto you

verses.original: Μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ἑαυτῆς ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: Mē oun merimnēsēte eis tēn aurion hē gar aurion merimnēsei heautēs arketon tē hēmera hē kakia autēs
verses.literal: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow for tomorrow will worry about itself Today has enough trouble of its own
